==English==

===Etymology===
1591, {{prefix|en|re|t1=back|imburse|t2=pay|lit2=put in a purse}} (perhaps after {{bor|en|frm|rembourser}} or {{bor|en|it|rimborsàre}}),<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=v|id=1006637566}}</ref> from {{der|en|frm|embourser}}, from {{der|en|fro|en-||in}} + {{m|fro|borser||to get money}}, from {{m|fro|borse||purse}}, from {{der|en|la-med|-}} {{m|fro|bursa}} ({{cog|en|purse}}).<ref>{{R:Online Etymology Dictionary}}</ref>

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˌɹiːɪmˈbɜː(ɹ)s/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-reimburse.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɜː(ɹ)s|s=3}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[compensate]] (someone) with [[payment]]; especially, to repay money spent on someone's [[behalf]].
#: {{synonyms|en|imburse|q1=one sense, obsolete}}
#: {{ux|en|The company will '''reimburse''' you for your expenses for the business trip.}}
#* {{quote-av
|en
|url=https://ia800705.us.archive.org/33/items/Penn_Radio_archive/The.Penn.Jillette.Radio.Show.2006.05.09.mp3
|time=15:35
|quotee=Rudy
|date=May 09, 2006
|title=w:Penn Radio
|author=w:Penn Jillette; w:Michael Goudeau
|text=You can tell this funny monkey story, but please keep and mind and tell people that the man who lost all his fruit to the monkeys was entirely '''reimbursed'''.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[recoup]] (funds spent).
#* {{RQ:Bramah Eyes of Max Carrados|passage=He has spent many years on the automaton, and it must have cost thousands of pounds in experiment and construction. He makes no secret of hoping to '''reimburse''' his outlay.}}

====Hypernyms====
